title: True or False: The Product Owner is allowed to adjust the Definition of Done during the Sprint to accommodate incomplete work. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done ensures that each Increment meets the Scrum Team’s quality standards and should not be altered during a Sprint to accommodate incomplete work. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a shared agreement and should not be adjusted to fit current work; it maintains quality standards.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done should remain consistent to ensure quality and transparency across the Increment.

title: A critical bug is discovered mid-Sprint that impacts the product’s core functionality. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to prioritize and address critical bugs within the current Sprint to maintain product functionality and quality. “Developers are responsible for turning Product Backlog items into Increments of value each Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Wait until the next Sprint to address the bug to maintain the current focus.
explanation1: Incorrect: Critical issues that impact core functionality should be addressed immediately to ensure product integrity.
answer2: Work with the Developers to prioritize the bug fix within the current Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing critical bugs promptly ensures that the product remains functional and reliable.
answer3: Delay the fix until it can be scheduled in a future Sprint to avoid disrupting the current Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying critical fixes compromises product quality and stakeholder trust.
answer4: Escalate the bug to management for immediate intervention.
explanation4: Incorrect: Critical issues should be managed by the Scrum Team without external escalation unless absolutely necessary.

title: The Product Owner notices that some Product Backlog items consistently fail to meet the Definition of Done. What is the best course of action? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to understand why items are not meeting the Definition of Done, helping to ensure quality and continuous improvement. “If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Lower the Definition of Done to match the team's current performance.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards compromises the integrity of the product and should be avoided.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to understand the issues and refine the Backlog items accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Working with the team to address why items aren't meeting the Definition of Done helps improve processes and outcomes.
answer3: Remove the items from the Product Backlog to simplify the team’s workload.
explanation3: Incorrect: Removing items does not address the underlying issues with meeting the Definition of Done.
answer4: Delay the incomplete work to the next Sprint without further discussion.
explanation4: Incorrect: Delaying work without understanding and addressing issues can lead to recurring problems.

title: Which two actions are necessary for the Development Team to ensure continuous delivery of high-quality Increments? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Adhering to the Definition of Done and conducting continuous code reviews and testing are crucial actions for ensuring high-quality Increments. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Adhering to the Definition of Done for all tasks completed.
explanation1: Correct: Adherence to the Definition of Done ensures that each Increment meets the agreed quality standards.
answer2: Conducting code reviews and automated testing throughout the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous testing and reviews help identify defects early, maintaining quality and reducing rework.
answer3: Completing all tasks as quickly as possible to maximize output.
explanation3: Incorrect: Speed without focus on quality can lead to substandard work and technical debt.
answer4: Only testing at the end of the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Testing should be integrated continuously, not just at the end.
answer5: Allowing the Product Owner to sign off on completed work.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner assesses value, but quality is maintained by the team's adherence to the Definition of Done.

title: Which three factors contribute most to the self-organizing nature of a Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Self-organization in Scrum Teams is supported by cross-functional skills, a culture of respect, and the ability to decide how to accomplish their work. “Self-managing teams choose who, how, and when their work gets done.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Clear boundaries of authority within the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: Scrum teams are self-organizing, meaning no external authority dictates their actions.
answer2: Cross-functional skills among team members.
explanation2: Correct: Cross-functionality ensures that the team has all the skills needed to complete their work without outside assistance.
answer3: A culture of collaboration and mutual respect.
explanation3: Correct: Collaboration and respect foster an environment where team members can self-manage effectively.
answer4: A Scrum Master who assigns tasks based on expertise.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates, but task assignment is up to the self-organizing team.
answer5: The ability to decide how to accomplish their work.
explanation5: Correct: The freedom to determine how they work supports the team’s autonomy and self-organization.

title: During a Daily Scrum, the Developers identify a risk that might impact the Sprint Goal. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the discussion, helping the Developers find the best approach to address the risk while keeping focus on the Sprint Goal. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Direct the team on how to handle the risk immediately.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not dictate how the team manages risks.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to help the team decide the best approach to manage the risk.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master facilitates the team's decision-making process, enabling them to handle risks effectively.
answer3: Ignore the risk to maintain focus on the current plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Risks should be addressed promptly to avoid impacting the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to adjust the Sprint Goal to accommodate the risk.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adjusting the Sprint Goal should be a last resort; the team should first explore ways to manage the risk.

title: During the Daily Scrum, the team reports that they are behind schedule on completing the Sprint Goal. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the team’s discussion on how to adjust their work, supporting them in making necessary adaptations to achieve the Sprint Goal. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Tell the team to work overtime to catch up.
explanation1: Incorrect: Forcing overtime can lead to burnout and does not align with Scrum’s principles of sustainable pace.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to help the team identify adjustments that can be made to achieve the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating discussions helps the team self-manage and find solutions to get back on track.
answer3: Ignore the issue and proceed as planned.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring issues prevents timely course correction and may lead to Sprint failure.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to remove some tasks to make the workload lighter.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adjustments should be decided by the team based on their inspection and adaptation processes.

title: True or False: The Product Owner can change the order of the Product Backlog at any time based on new stakeholder feedback. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner continuously refines and orders the Product Backlog to align with the latest stakeholder feedback and market conditions, ensuring the product remains valuable. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for managing and ordering the Product Backlog to maximize value and can adjust it as needed.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner must adapt the Product Backlog based on new insights to ensure it delivers maximum value.

title: True or False: The Scrum Master decides the order of items in the Product Backlog. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is accountable for managing the Product Backlog, including prioritizing items to maximize value. “The Product Owner is the sole person responsible for managing the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for ordering the Product Backlog based on value and priorities.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner manages the order of items in the Product Backlog based on value considerations.

title: Which two strategies should the Product Owner use to keep the Product Backlog aligned with market needs? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage with stakeholders regularly and use data-driven prioritization to keep the Product Backlog aligned with evolving market needs and deliver maximum value. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Only update the Product Backlog during formal events like Sprint Reviews.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously updated to reflect new insights and feedback, not just during formal events.
answer2: Regularly engage with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust the Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous engagement ensures the Product Backlog remains aligned with current market needs.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on high-value items.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help prioritize work that delivers the most value to the product and stakeholders.
answer4: Ignore minor feedback to maintain focus on the current Product Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to keep the Product Backlog adaptable and responsive.
answer5: Delegate Backlog updates to the Developers to maintain focus on other tasks.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for Backlog management and should be actively involved.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take when the Product Backlog is consistently not delivering the expected value? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders and use data-driven insights to ensure the Product Backlog is consistently delivering value and aligned with current needs. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Continue with the current priorities to maintain stability.
explanation1: Incorrect: Maintaining the status quo when value is not being delivered does not address the issue.
answer2: Engage stakeholders to gather new insights and adjust the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Stakeholder engagement helps align the Product Backlog with current needs and market conditions.
answer3: Use data to re-evaluate the value of Product Backlog items and reprioritize accordingly.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven prioritization ensures the Product Backlog is focused on delivering the highest value.
answer4: Delegate Backlog management to the Developers to improve value.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing the Product Backlog and ensuring value delivery.
answer5: Ignore stakeholder feedback to maintain the current direction.
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback is essential for keeping the Product Backlog relevant and value-driven.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take to ensure the Product Backlog remains up-to-date and valuable? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage with stakeholders regularly and use data-driven prioritization to ensure the Product Backlog remains relevant, up-to-date, and valuable. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Update the Product Backlog only during formal Scrum events.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously refined and updated based on new insights and needs.
answer2: Regularly engage with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous engagement helps keep the Backlog aligned with evolving needs and priorities.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on high-value items.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help maintain a Backlog that delivers the most value to the product.
answer4: Ignore minor feedback to avoid constant changes to the Backlog.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to ensure the Backlog remains adaptable and relevant.
answer5: Delegate Backlog management to the Scrum Master to streamline updates.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for managing and updating the Product Backlog.

title: Which three activities should the Product Owner engage in to ensure the Product Backlog remains aligned with stakeholder needs? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner must actively engage with stakeholders, adjust to market conditions, and prioritize work based on value to maintain a relevant Product Backlog. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Regularly meeting with stakeholders to gather feedback.
explanation1: Correct: Continuous engagement ensures that the Product Backlog reflects current needs and priorities.
answer2: Delegating stakeholder meetings to the Scrum Master.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for stakeholder engagement.
answer3: Analyzing market changes to adjust the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: Adapting to market changes ensures the product stays competitive.
answer4: Collaborating with Developers to refine technical aspects.
explanation4: Incorrect: Technical refinements are primarily the responsibility of the Developers.
answer5: Prioritizing items based on potential value delivery.
explanation5: Correct: Prioritizing for value ensures the most impactful work is done first.

title: Which three actions are crucial for the Product Owner to effectively manage the Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective Backlog management requires the Product Owner to engage with stakeholders, prioritize based on value, and keep the Backlog updated. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Engaging with stakeholders regularly to gather feedback.
explanation1: Correct: Regular engagement ensures the Product Backlog reflects the needs of stakeholders.
answer2: Delegating Backlog refinement to Developers.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for refinement, though they work collaboratively with the team.
answer3: Prioritizing items based on business value.
explanation3: Correct: Prioritization ensures the most valuable work is done first, aligning with business goals.
answer4: Only focusing on items for the next Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner must think ahead and keep the entire Backlog ready.
answer5: Updating the Backlog frequently based on emerging insights.
explanation5: Correct: Keeping the Backlog updated ensures it remains relevant and valuable.

title: A Product Owner notices that the Product Backlog is not being refined regularly, causing delays. What is the best course of action? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should ensure that regular refinement sessions occur to keep the Product Backlog up to date and ready for future Sprints. This helps maintain focus and alignment within the team. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Schedule mandatory refinement sessions with the team to ensure regular updates.
explanation1: Correct: Regular refinement sessions help keep the Product Backlog updated and manageable.
answer2: Ignore the issue and focus on completing the current Sprint.
explanation2: Incorrect: Ignoring refinement issues can lead to further delays and misalignment.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to take over the refinement process.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for refinement, though it is a collaborative process.
answer4: Delay the Sprint until the Backlog is fully refined.
explanation4: Incorrect: Delaying a Sprint disrupts the team’s workflow and should be avoided.

title: During a Sprint, the Product Owner receives a request to change the priority of a key feature. What is the best action? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate the change request and manage it through the Product Backlog, maintaining focus on the Sprint Goal. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Change the priority immediately to address the request.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changing priorities mid-Sprint disrupts focus and alignment with the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Evaluate the request and update the Product Backlog for future prioritization.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner manages changes through the Product Backlog, ensuring the current Sprint remains focused.
answer3: Reject the request to keep the Sprint on track.
explanation3: Incorrect: Requests should be evaluated, not dismissed outright.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the stakeholder’s concerns.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing the Product Backlog and stakeholder feedback is the Product Owner's responsibility.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies a pattern of frequent miscommunications about Product Backlog items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively work with the Developers to refine unclear Backlog items, ensuring they are ready and well-understood for future Sprints. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback and maintain the current refinement process.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback prevents improvement and can perpetuate misunderstandings.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to improve refinement, ensuring clarity and understanding of Backlog items.
explanation2: Correct: Enhancing refinement processes helps ensure Backlog items are clear and actionable for future Sprints.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to manage refinement issues independently.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refinement and should actively participate in clarifying Backlog items.
answer4: Delay addressing these issues until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement improvements should be addressed continuously, not delayed until planning sessions.

title: True or False: The Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint if it no longer makes sense in the context of the product's value. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and it is usually due to significant changes in value or goals. Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner can cancel a Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete or irrelevant.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is the only role with the authority to cancel a Sprint based on value considerations.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is the only person who can cancel a Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is the only individual with the authority to cancel a Sprint, as they are responsible for managing the value of the work done by the Scrum Team. “A Sprint can be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete or is no longer valuable.
explanation2: Incorrect: Although other stakeholders may advise, only the Product Owner can make the decision to cancel the Sprint.

title: What are the two primary responsibilities of the Product Owner during a Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes product value by refining the Product Backlog and engaging stakeholders. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Prioritizing the work done during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Work during the Sprint should already be prioritized.
answer2: Collaborating with stakeholders and customers.
explanation2: Correct: Engaging stakeholders helps ensure the product meets market needs.
answer3: Attending every Daily Scrum to monitor progress.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not need to attend every Daily Scrum.
answer4: Refining and managing the Product Backlog.
explanation4: Correct: Ongoing Backlog refinement is a key responsibility of the Product Owner.
answer5: Directing developers on how to implement items.
explanation5: Incorrect: Developers are self-managing in how they implement items.

title: Which three responsibilities are specific to the Product Owner role in Scrum? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner’s responsibilities include managing the Product Backlog, defining the Sprint Goal with the team, and engaging stakeholders to ensure the product meets their needs. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Managing and prioritizing the Product Backlog.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for ensuring the Product Backlog reflects current priorities and maximizes product value.
answer2: Defining the Sprint Goal alongside the Scrum Team.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner collaborates with the team to set a Sprint Goal that aligns with product objectives.
answer3: Engaging with stakeholders to gather feedback and requirements.
explanation3: Correct: Regular engagement ensures that the Product Owner understands stakeholder needs and adjusts the Product Backlog accordingly.
answer4: Approving the work completed by the Development Team.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner assesses value but does not approve individual tasks; that responsibility lies with the Definition of Done.
answer5: Facilitating the Daily Scrum.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates Scrum events, not the Product Owner.

title: Which three actions should the Product Owner take if multiple stakeholders have conflicting priorities? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively engage with stakeholders, use data to inform decisions, and communicate transparently to resolve priority conflicts. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management, which includes ordering items to best achieve goals and missions.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Meet with stakeholders to understand their needs and concerns.
explanation1: Correct: Engaging with stakeholders helps the Product Owner understand different priorities and make informed decisions.
answer2: Ask the Scrum Master to resolve the conflict.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner, not the Scrum Master, manages stakeholder engagement and prioritization.
answer3: Use data and metrics to assess the value of each request.
explanation3: Correct: Using data helps to make objective prioritization decisions based on value.
answer4: Defer all conflicting requests to future Sprints.
explanation4: Incorrect: Deferring conflicts does not resolve the issue and can lead to stakeholder dissatisfaction.
answer5: Clearly communicate the prioritization decisions and rationale to stakeholders.
explanation5: Correct: Transparency in decision-making helps manage expectations and fosters trust.

title: The Product Owner frequently requests changes during the Sprint that affect the Sprint Goal. How should the Development Team handle these requests? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Development Team should work closely with the Product Owner to assess the impact of requested changes on the Sprint Goal and adjust their focus as needed. “During the Sprint, scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Accept all changes to keep the Product Owner happy.
explanation1: Incorrect: Accepting changes without considering their impact on the Sprint Goal can lead to chaos and missed objectives.
answer2: Collaborate with the Product Owner to re-evaluate the Sprint Goal and adjust if necessary.
explanation2: Correct: Working with the Product Owner allows the team to re-align their focus and maintain a realistic Sprint Goal.
answer3: Reject any changes once the Sprint has started.
explanation3: Incorrect: Blanket rejection is not collaborative; dialogue with the Product Owner is necessary.
answer4: Delay all changes until the Sprint Review.
explanation4: Incorrect: Waiting until the Sprint Review to address changes can lead to misalignment and missed opportunities.

title: During a Sprint Planning session, the Development Team is unsure about the expected outcome of a particular Product Backlog item. What should they do to gain clarity? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is responsible for clarifying Product Backlog items during Sprint Planning to ensure the team can effectively plan and commit to their work. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Proceed with the item and clarify details during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Starting work without clear understanding can lead to misunderstandings and rework.
answer2: Ask the Product Owner to clarify the item during Sprint Planning.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for clarifying Product Backlog items, ensuring the team understands what is expected.
answer3: Reassign the item to the next Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying work without attempting clarification reduces the team’s effectiveness in achieving the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Estimate the item with the assumption that details will become clear later.
explanation4: Incorrect: Estimating without understanding details leads to inaccurate planning and possible Sprint failure.

title: True or False: The Product Backlog is an artifact that supports the pillar of Transparency by making work visible to everyone involved. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog supports the pillar of Transparency by making all future work visible, allowing stakeholders to understand what is planned. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Product Backlog is a transparent artifact that shows all future work needed to achieve the Product Goal.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Backlog is designed to provide visibility into all planned work.

title: Which three components of the Sprint Backlog provide a complete view of the work for the Sprint? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog includes the Sprint Goal, the tasks to complete, and the team’s plan, providing a full overview of the work needed to achieve the Sprint objectives. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: The Sprint Goal
explanation1: Correct: The Sprint Goal provides a clear objective that guides the Development Team’s work.
answer2: The list of tasks the team commits to completing during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: These tasks outline the work necessary to achieve the Sprint Goal.
answer3: The Definition of Done
explanation3: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but is not part of the Sprint Backlog.
answer4: Progress tracking tools like Burndown Charts
explanation4: Incorrect: These tools help track progress but are not part of the Sprint Backlog.
answer5: The team’s plan for achieving the Sprint Goal
explanation5: Correct: This plan details how the Development Team intends to accomplish their work during the Sprint.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take when the team struggles with the Definition of Done? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine the Definition of Done and improve refinement practices, ensuring quality standards are met. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the issue to maintain the Sprint’s pace.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring quality issues compromises the product’s integrity.
answer2: Work with the team to refine the Definition of Done and ensure it is achievable.
explanation2: Correct: Collaborating to refine the Definition of Done helps the team meet quality standards consistently.
answer3: Encourage the team to lower the Definition of Done temporarily.
explanation3: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards undermines the product’s value.
answer4: Facilitate discussions to identify areas where refinement practices can be improved.
explanation4: Correct: Improving refinement helps ensure that Product Backlog items meet the Definition of Done consistently.
answer5: Assign the Scrum Master to enforce adherence to the Definition of Done.
explanation5: Incorrect: Adherence to the Definition of Done is a shared responsibility of the Scrum Team.

title: During Backlog Refinement, the Development Team struggles to understand a complex item. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should provide additional details to ensure the Development Team fully understands complex items, facilitating effective refinement and planning. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Skip the item and move on to the next one to save time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Skipping items without clarification can lead to misunderstandings and ineffective Sprint Planning.
answer2: Ask the Product Owner to provide additional details and context.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for clarifying Product Backlog items to ensure the team fully understands the work.
answer3: Estimate the item conservatively and proceed with limited understanding.
explanation3: Incorrect: Estimating without full understanding increases risk and may result in incomplete or incorrect work.
answer4: Defer the item to a future refinement session when more information is available.
explanation4: Incorrect: Delaying understanding can cause bottlenecks and reduce planning effectiveness.

title: Which artifact directly supports the Scrum pillar of Adaptation by allowing the team to make informed decisions during the Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog supports the pillar of Adaptation by providing the team with a clear plan that they can adjust as new information emerges during the Sprint. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog guides future work but does not directly support ongoing adaptation within a Sprint.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog helps the team adapt their work during the Sprint based on new information.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment shows completed work but does not directly support adaptation during the Sprint.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality but does not directly facilitate ongoing adaptation.

title: Which artifact provides transparency into what work has been completed and demonstrates progress toward the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment represents the work completed during the Sprint and serves as a measure of progress toward the Product Goal. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog shows planned work for the Sprint but does not reflect completed progress.
answer2: Increment
explanation2: Correct: The Increment shows all completed work, providing visibility into progress toward the Product Goal.
answer3: Product Backlog
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists future work but does not directly show completed progress.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality standards but does not provide insight into completed work.

title: True or False: The Product Owner has the authority to change the Sprint Goal during the Sprint if new information emerges. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Goal is set during Sprint Planning and provides a single objective for the Sprint, which should not change once the Sprint begins. “The Sprint Goal is an objective set for the Sprint that can be met through the implementation of Product Backlog items.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Once the Sprint begins, the Sprint Goal is fixed and cannot be changed; it provides direction and focus for the team.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal remains constant during the Sprint to maintain focus and guide the Development Team’s efforts.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is required to attend every Sprint Retrospective to monitor team performance. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner participates in the Sprint Retrospective to collaborate with the Scrum Team on identifying improvements, not to monitor individual performance. “The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Retrospective is not a performance review; it is focused on improving the team's processes.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner participates in the Retrospective as a team member, contributing to discussions on improvements.

title: Which three elements are essential for a successful Sprint Planning meeting? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Successful Sprint Planning involves setting a clear Sprint Goal, obtaining input from the Product Owner, and identifying risks to manage expectations and ensure alignment. “The Sprint Goal is an objective set for the Sprint that can be met through the implementation of Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: A clear and well-defined Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Correct: A clear Sprint Goal provides direction and focus for the team throughout the Sprint.
answer2: The Product Owner’s input on what needs to be achieved.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner’s input ensures that the most valuable work is prioritized and understood by the team.
answer3: Accurate time estimates for each task.
explanation3: Incorrect: Scrum focuses on estimating effort rather than exact time, allowing the team flexibility in task execution.
answer4: Identification of potential risks that could impact the Sprint.
explanation4: Correct: Identifying risks helps the team plan effectively and anticipate challenges.
answer5: The Scrum Master assigning tasks to team members.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Development Team self-organizes and decides how to accomplish their work; tasks are not assigned by the Scrum Master.

title: Which two events in Scrum provide formal opportunities to inspect and adapt the Product Increment and processes ? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective are key events for inspecting and adapting the Increment and team processes, ensuring continuous improvement. “Scrum Events are designed to enable critical transparency and inspection.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Retrospective
explanation1: Correct: The Retrospective adapts team processes.
answer2: Sprint Review
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review inspects the Increment and adapts the Product Backlog
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is focused on day-to-day progress, not the Increment.
answer4: Sprint Planning
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprint Planning do not inspect the Increment directly
answer5: Definition of Done
explanation5: Incorrect: While the Definition of Done ensures quality, it is not an event that adapts the Increment.

title: A stakeholder complains about the quality of the product during the Sprint Review. What is the best response from the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should acknowledge stakeholder feedback and work with the team to refine the Definition of Done, ensuring quality improvements in future Increments. “The Sprint Review is a working session to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defend the team’s work and move on to the next topic.
explanation1: Incorrect: Dismissing stakeholder feedback can damage trust and hinder product improvement.
answer2: Acknowledge the feedback and discuss ways to improve the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: Acknowledging feedback and refining quality standards helps address concerns and improve future Increments.
answer3: Ignore the complaint to avoid conflict during the meeting.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines the purpose of the Sprint Review.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the stakeholder’s complaint separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should directly address product feedback during the Sprint Review.

title: The Development Team is experiencing communication issues, leading to misunderstandings about task responsibilities. What should they do to resolve this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum is an essential opportunity for the Development Team to align on their work, improve communication, and ensure that responsibilities are clear. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Schedule additional meetings to clarify responsibilities.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding more meetings may lead to overcommunication and does not directly solve the problem.
answer2: Use the Daily Scrum to improve communication and ensure alignment on tasks.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum provides an opportunity to discuss progress, clarify responsibilities, and align the team’s efforts.
answer3: Assign a team lead to manage communication between members.
explanation3: Incorrect: Assigning a lead undermines the self-organizing nature of the Development Team.
answer4: Rely on the Scrum Master to manage communication within the team.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not manage team communication; the team is self-organizing.

title: The team frequently misses Sprint Goals due to unclear task requirements. Which Scrum event should be used to address and improve this situation? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Backlog Refinement sessions help the Scrum Team clarify Product Backlog items, ensuring that tasks are well understood before being pulled into a Sprint. “Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing process of keeping the backlog items in good order.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Review
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review focuses on the Increment and stakeholder feedback, not task clarification.
answer2: Backlog Refinement
explanation2: Correct: Backlog Refinement is used to clarify task requirements, ensuring items are ready for upcoming Sprints.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum inspects progress but does not focus on clarifying future tasks.
answer4: Sprint Retrospective
explanation4: Incorrect: The Retrospective addresses team processes but does not specifically clarify task requirements.

title: Which pillar of Scrum is best supported by the Definition of Done? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Inspection is supported by the Definition of Done, as it provides a clear standard for assessing the completeness and quality of each Increment. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Transparency
explanation1: Incorrect: Transparency is supported by clear communication, but the Definition of Done specifically enhances Inspection.
answer2: Inspection
explanation2: Correct: A clear Definition of Done ensures that each Increment can be properly inspected for quality and completeness.
answer3: Adaptation
explanation3: Incorrect: Adaptation occurs after inspection, but the Definition of Done does not directly support it.
answer4: Courage
explanation4: Incorrect: Courage is a value, not a pillar supported by the Definition of Done.

title: Which three pillars of Scrum are demonstrated when the team inspects and adapts their work processes regularly? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The pillars of Transparency, Inspection, and Adaptation are fundamental to Scrum, enabling the team to continually improve their work processes. “These three pillars require trust to operate effectively.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Inspection
explanation1: Correct: Regularly inspecting work processes helps the team identify areas for improvement.
answer2: Transparency
explanation2: Correct: Transparency allows everyone to see the work process clearly, enabling effective inspection and adaptation.
answer3: Commitment
explanation3: Incorrect: While Commitment is a value, it is not a pillar that directly facilitates inspection and adaptation.
answer4: Adaptation
explanation4: Correct: Adaptation ensures that the team can make necessary adjustments based on their inspections.
answer5: Courage
explanation5: Incorrect: Courage is a Scrum value, not a pillar.

title: Which three tools or techniques help Scrum Teams ensure that their work meets the agreed quality standards? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Tools like the Definition of Done, Daily Scrums, and Backlog Refinement ensure that the team maintains quality throughout the development process. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Using a Definition of Done that includes all quality requirements.
explanation1: Correct: The Definition of Done ensures that all work meets the agreed-upon quality standards before it is considered complete.
answer2: Conducting thorough testing only at the end of the Sprint.
explanation2: Incorrect: Testing should be integrated throughout the Sprint to ensure continuous quality.
answer3: Daily Scrums that focus on current progress and blockers.
explanation3: Correct: Daily Scrums help the team inspect their work and adjust their efforts to maintain quality and progress.
answer4: Frequent Backlog Refinement sessions to clarify requirements.
explanation4: Correct: Refining the Backlog helps ensure that items are well understood and meet the team’s standards before entering a Sprint.
answer5: Skipping Retrospectives to avoid wasting time on discussions.
explanation5: Incorrect: Retrospectives are critical for continuous improvement and maintaining quality.

title: Which two tools can help the Scrum Team maintain focus on completing work that directly contributes to the Sprint Goal? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog and Sprint Goal help the team maintain focus on what needs to be done to achieve the Sprint Goal, ensuring alignment and efficient task management. “The Sprint Backlog is the set of Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog and Definition of Done
explanation1: Correct: The Sprint Backlog contains tasks that align with the Sprint Goal, and the Definition of Done ensures quality.
answer2: Daily Scrum and Sprint Retrospective
explanation2: Incorrect: These events help inspect progress and improve processes but do not directly guide task focus.
answer3: Burndown Chart and Velocity
explanation3: Incorrect: These are used for tracking progress and capacity but do not directly influence task focus.
answer4: Product Backlog and Increment
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog prioritizes future work, and the Increment shows completed work, not current task focus.
answer5: Sprint Goal and Task Board
explanation5: Correct: The Sprint Goal provides direction, and the Task Board visualizes progress, helping maintain focus.

title: During a Sprint, the Development Team frequently finds itself blocked by dependencies that are not being resolved. Which Scrum technique or tool could help address this issue in future Sprints? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Impediment Backlog helps Scrum Teams track and prioritize unresolved issues that block progress, ensuring that dependencies are managed proactively in future Sprints. “Scrum Teams identify impediments and prioritize removing them.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Retrospective
explanation1: Incorrect: The Retrospective helps reflect on the Sprint but does not specifically address dependency management.
answer2: Impediment Backlog
explanation2: Correct: Creating an Impediment Backlog helps track and prioritize unresolved issues, including dependencies.
answer3: Burndown Chart
explanation3: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks progress but does not address specific impediments.
answer4: Backlog Refinement
explanation4: Incorrect: Backlog Refinement improves clarity and readiness of items but does not manage impediments.

title: During the Daily Scrum, the team frequently discusses the same impediments without resolution. What tool could they introduce to help track and manage these issues more effectively? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: An Impediment Log allows the team to document, track, and prioritize issues that block progress, ensuring they are managed proactively. “Scrum Teams actively manage impediments to progress.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Burndown Chart
explanation1: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks progress but does not manage impediments specifically.
answer2: Impediment Log
explanation2: Correct: An Impediment Log helps track and prioritize issues, ensuring that the team actively manages and resolves them.
answer3: Task Board
explanation3: Incorrect: A Task Board shows the status of tasks but does not specifically track impediments.
answer4: Definition of Ready
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Ready ensures tasks are prepared for the Sprint but does not track impediments.

title: The Product Owner is often unavailable during Sprint Planning, causing delays in defining the Sprint Goal. What tool or technique can help the team mitigate this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Pre-Sprint Refinement sessions help ensure that Backlog items are well-defined and ready, reducing the need for extensive Product Owner involvement during Sprint Planning. “Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity to keep the Product Backlog updated and ready.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Burndown Chart
explanation1: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks progress but does not assist with Sprint Planning.
answer2: Pre-Sprint Backlog Refinement Sessions
explanation2: Correct: Pre-Sprint Refinement sessions ensure Backlog items are ready, reducing dependency on the Product Owner during Sprint Planning.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum helps inspect progress but does not address Sprint Planning issues.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets standards for task completion but does not assist with availability issues.

title: The team is using Planning Poker to estimate tasks, but some team members feel pressured to conform to others' estimates. What adjustment can be made to improve this situation? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Using silent estimation rounds before group discussion in Planning Poker helps reduce conformity pressure, allowing each team member to provide their honest input. “Estimation helps the Scrum Team understand the effort required to achieve the Sprint Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Switch to Story Points for estimation.
explanation1: Incorrect: Story Points are an estimation unit, not a method that addresses conformity issues.
answer2: Use silent estimation rounds before discussion.
explanation2: Correct: Silent estimation encourages individual input before group discussion, reducing conformity pressure.
answer3: Have the Scrum Master assign estimates based on their judgment.
explanation3: Incorrect: Estimates should be team-driven, not assigned by the Scrum Master.
answer4: Skip estimation and start the work immediately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Estimation helps the team plan effectively; skipping it undermines planning accuracy.

title: Which Scrum value is most emphasized when the team adapts their work plan in response to new challenges? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Courage is emphasized when the team adapts their work plan, empowering them to take bold actions in response to new challenges. “Scrum’s success is based on people becoming more proficient in living five values.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Courage
explanation1: Correct: Courage enables the team to adapt and make necessary changes when faced with challenges.
answer2: Openness
explanation2: Incorrect: Openness supports transparency but does not directly drive the adaptation of work plans.
answer3: Respect
explanation3: Incorrect: Respect fosters collaboration, but Courage is crucial for taking bold actions to adapt.
answer4: Focus
explanation4: Incorrect: Focus helps maintain direction, but Courage drives the willingness to adapt when needed.

title: True or False: The Product Owner can cancel the Sprint if it is clear that the Sprint Goal cannot be met. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes irrelevant, ensuring the team's work aligns with the highest value goals. “A Sprint can be canceled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner has the authority to cancel the Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
explanation2: Incorrect: Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint when the Sprint Goal no longer holds value.

title: True or False: The Product Owner must cancel the Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes impossible to achieve. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, but this decision should be considered carefully. “A Sprint can be canceled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is a decision that should be made carefully and not solely based on the Sprint Goal being unachievable.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner may cancel the Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, but it is not mandatory.

title: During a Sprint, the Developers realize they will not complete all Product Backlog items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: If the team cannot complete all items, the Product Owner should help refocus efforts on the most valuable work, ensuring maximum value is still delivered. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Extend the Sprint to allow time to complete the work.
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprint durations are fixed and should not be extended.
answer2: Work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog and focus on the most valuable items.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should help prioritize the remaining work to maximize value within the Sprint.
answer3: Reassign incomplete work to another team.
explanation3: Incorrect: Incomplete work should remain within the current team’s Product Backlog.
answer4: Cancel the Sprint due to the inability to meet the forecast.
explanation4: Incorrect: Cancelling a Sprint is a last resort and should not be used for scope adjustments.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers express uncertainty about the feasibility of the Sprint Goal. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring that the Sprint Goal remains achievable and valuable. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Insist that the team commits to the Sprint Goal regardless of concerns.
explanation1: Incorrect: Insisting on unrealistic commitments can lead to failure and decreased morale.
answer2: Work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog and ensure the goal is achievable.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog helps align team efforts with a realistic and valuable Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ignore the concerns to maintain focus on the original plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Addressing concerns ensures the team’s commitment and capability to meet the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to enforce the Sprint Goal as planned.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should actively participate in aligning the Sprint Goal with achievable work.

title: During the Sprint, the Product Owner finds that the team is struggling to meet the Sprint Goal due to new technical challenges. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring that the team remains focused on the most valuable work despite challenges. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Encourage the team to push through and complete all the work as planned.
explanation1: Incorrect: Pushing the team to work harder without addressing the issues can lead to burnout and decreased quality.
answer2: Work with the team to adjust the Sprint Backlog, focusing on the most valuable work.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog helps refocus efforts on achievable, high-value items while maintaining the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Cancel the Sprint to restart with a more realistic plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint should only be considered if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
answer4: Ignore the problem and continue with the current plan.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring issues can lead to unmet goals and reduced value delivery.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers realize that a high-priority item is too complex to complete within the Sprint. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine or split complex items, making them manageable and ready for the current or future Sprints. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Include the item anyway to maintain the priority.
explanation1: Incorrect: Including complex items without refinement can jeopardize the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Work with the Developers to refine the item or split it into smaller, manageable tasks.
explanation2: Correct: Refining or splitting complex items ensures they are actionable and achievable within the Sprint.
answer3: Move the item to the next Sprint without changes.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying work without addressing complexity does not solve the problem.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to facilitate the refinement process.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for leading refinement with the Developers.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders express concerns that the Increment does not fully meet their expectations. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders during the Sprint Review to gather feedback and update the Product Backlog, ensuring future work aligns with expectations. “The Sprint Review is an opportunity to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defend the Increment by highlighting the challenges faced by the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: Defending work without addressing feedback does not build trust or improve future outcomes.
answer2: Engage with stakeholders to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should manage feedback actively and refine the Backlog to better align with stakeholder needs.
answer3: Ignore the concerns and focus on the existing Product Backlog priorities.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines the purpose of stakeholder engagement and the Sprint Review.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to address stakeholder concerns separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing stakeholder feedback and refining the Product Backlog.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders provide feedback that contradicts the current Product Goal. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders and the Scrum Team to evaluate feedback and determine how it impacts the Product Goal and Product Backlog. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately change the Product Goal to align with stakeholder feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changing the Product Goal without proper evaluation can misalign the product’s direction.
answer2: Discuss the feedback with the Scrum Team and stakeholders to assess its impact on the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should evaluate feedback collaboratively and make necessary adjustments to the Backlog.
answer3: Ignore the feedback to maintain focus on the existing Product Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: Feedback should be considered and evaluated to ensure the Product Backlog remains relevant.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the stakeholder expectations.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for engaging stakeholders and managing the Product Backlog.

title: During the Sprint, a stakeholder requests a status update on a specific feature. What is the best way for the Product Owner to respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should provide a concise update to the stakeholder, ensuring they understand the current progress and how it aligns with the Product Goal. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Provide a detailed status report immediately to satisfy the stakeholder.
explanation1: Incorrect: Detailed reports can take time away from managing the Product Backlog and prioritizing work.
answer2: Refer the stakeholder to the Sprint Review, where progress will be demonstrated.
explanation2: Incorrect: Sprint Reviews are not the only opportunity to update stakeholders on progress.
answer3: Engage with the stakeholder to provide a concise update and explain how the feature aligns with the Product Goal.
explanation3: Correct: Engaging with stakeholders and explaining the progress ensures transparency and alignment.
answer4: Ignore the request and focus on managing the Product Backlog.
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholder engagement is crucial for maintaining trust and alignment with business goals.

title: Which three actions should the Product Owner take to improve collaboration with stakeholders? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders regularly, use data-driven communication, and seek feedback proactively to ensure ongoing alignment and collaboration. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Meet with stakeholders only during the Sprint Review to gather feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: Regular engagement is essential for maintaining alignment with stakeholder needs.
answer2: Involve stakeholders in Product Backlog refinement sessions when appropriate.
explanation2: Correct: Including stakeholders in refinement sessions helps align the Product Backlog with market needs and feedback.
answer3: Use clear, data-driven communication to explain prioritization decisions.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven communication fosters transparency and helps stakeholders understand why certain decisions are made.
answer4: Delegate stakeholder communication to the Scrum Master to streamline the process.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should maintain direct communication with stakeholders to ensure clear alignment.
answer5: Proactively seek feedback throughout the Sprint cycle, not just at formal events.
explanation5: Correct: Continuous feedback helps the Product Owner make informed decisions and maintain a relevant Product Backlog.

title: During the Sprint, the Developers encounter a significant technical challenge. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the discussion, helping the Developers find the best approach to address the challenge while keeping focus on the Sprint Goal. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Solve the technical challenge for the team to keep progress on track.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates problem-solving but does not solve technical challenges for the team.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to help the Developers decide on the best approach to handle the challenge.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master enables the team to self-manage and resolve challenges effectively.
answer3: Ignore the challenge to maintain focus on the current plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Challenges should be addressed promptly to avoid disrupting the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to reprioritize other items to accommodate the challenge.
explanation4: Incorrect: The focus should be on resolving the challenge, not reprioritizing work without addressing the issue.

title: Which concept in Scrum helps ensure that the team delivers Increments of high quality consistently? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done ensures that all completed work meets a shared standard of quality before it is considered finished. “The Definition of Done is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Planning
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprint Planning sets the Sprint Goal but does not specifically ensure Increment quality.
answer2: Scrum Artifacts
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done provides a clear standard for quality, ensuring that all Increments meet the agreed-upon criteria.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum helps inspect progress but does not define quality standards.
answer4: Sprint Backlog
explanation4: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog lists the work but does not define quality standards.

title: During a Sprint, a stakeholder asks the Product Owner to add an urgent feature. How should the Product Owner respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate the stakeholder’s request and add it to the Product Backlog for future consideration, keeping the current Sprint focused. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Add the feature immediately to keep the stakeholder happy.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding work mid-Sprint disrupts the focus and could jeopardize the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Evaluate the request and add it to the Product Backlog for future prioritization.
explanation2: Correct: Managing changes through the Product Backlog allows for prioritization without disrupting the current Sprint.
answer3: Reject the request outright to avoid disruptions.
explanation3: Incorrect: All requests should be considered and evaluated, not dismissed without discussion.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the request separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing changes and prioritizing the Product Backlog.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies frequent misunderstandings of Product Backlog items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively work with the Developers to refine Product Backlog items, ensuring they are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback to maintain the current refinement process.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback can lead to recurring misunderstandings and inefficiencies.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to improve refinement, ensuring items are clear and actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Improving refinement processes helps ensure that Product Backlog items are well understood by the team.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to manage refinement challenges independently.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refinement and should actively participate in clarifying Backlog items.
answer4: Delay addressing the feedback until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement improvements should be addressed continuously, not delayed.

title: During a Sprint Review, stakeholders request changes that could significantly alter the current Product Goal. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should assess feedback collaboratively with the Scrum Team and stakeholders to determine the impact on the Product Goal and Backlog. “The Product Owner is responsible for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately change the Product Goal to align with the new stakeholder requests.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changing the Product Goal without proper evaluation can disrupt the product's strategic direction.
answer2: Discuss the feedback with the Scrum Team and stakeholders to assess the impact on the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should collaborate to evaluate changes and adjust the Backlog accordingly.
answer3: Reject the changes to keep the current focus intact.
explanation3: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered and evaluated thoughtfully.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage stakeholder expectations.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing the Product Goal and stakeholder feedback.

title: During the Sprint, the Product Owner realizes that the Product Backlog is not aligned with stakeholder needs. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner must keep the Product Backlog updated based on stakeholder feedback to ensure it reflects the most current priorities and delivers value. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the issue until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation1: Incorrect: Delaying adjustments can result in further misalignment and lost value.
answer2: Update the Product Backlog continuously to reflect current stakeholder needs and feedback.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should continuously refine the Product Backlog based on new insights and feedback.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to prioritize stakeholder feedback for the next Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder feedback is the responsibility of the Product Owner.
answer4: Reprioritize all Backlog items immediately without consulting the team.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reprioritization should be done collaboratively and strategically, not impulsively.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take if the Product Backlog becomes unmanageable due to too many items? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with stakeholders to reprioritize and refine the Product Backlog, breaking down large items into actionable tasks to maintain focus and manageability. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Remove items without consulting stakeholders to streamline the Backlog.
explanation1: Incorrect: Removing items without stakeholder input can lead to misalignment with product goals.
answer2: Engage stakeholders to reprioritize and refine the Backlog, focusing on high-value items.
explanation2: Correct: Collaborating with stakeholders ensures the Product Backlog reflects the most current priorities.
answer3: Break down large items into smaller, more manageable tasks to maintain focus.
explanation3: Correct: Decomposing large items makes the Backlog more actionable and aligns work with team capacity.
answer4: Delay Backlog refinement until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement is an ongoing process and should not be delayed.
answer5: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the Product Backlog on behalf of the team.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for Backlog management, not the Scrum Master.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Product Owner's accountability for the Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner is accountable for managing the Product Backlog by engaging in continuous refinement, prioritization, and collaboration with the team. “The Product Owner is the sole person responsible for managing the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Allowing Developers to manage the Product Backlog independently.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for the Backlog and must ensure it is managed effectively.
answer2: Continuously refining and prioritizing items based on feedback and value.
explanation2: Correct: Ongoing refinement and prioritization ensure the Backlog reflects current priorities.
answer3: Collaborating with the team to ensure items are clear and actionable.
explanation3: Correct: Collaboration helps ensure the Product Backlog items are well understood and ready for future Sprints.
answer4: Using data to make informed decisions about prioritization.
explanation4: Correct: Data-driven decisions help align the Product Backlog with business goals and maximize value.
answer5: Only adjusting the Backlog during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement is an ongoing process, not limited to formal events.

title: What should the Product Owner do if stakeholders are unhappy with the direction of the Product Backlog? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should listen to stakeholder feedback and adjust the Product Backlog to ensure it remains aligned with value delivery expectations. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Reprioritize the Backlog immediately based on stakeholder feedback.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner should adjust the Backlog to ensure it aligns with stakeholder expectations and delivers value.
answer2: Ignore the feedback if it contradicts the current Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Incorrect: Feedback should always be considered and used to adapt the Backlog appropriately.
answer3: Request that the Scrum Master address the concerns with the stakeholders.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing stakeholder expectations and Backlog adjustments.
answer4: Delay changes until the next Sprint Planning.
explanation4: Incorrect: Backlog management is ongoing and does not need to wait for formal planning sessions.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Scrum Master's role in supporting the Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master supports the team by facilitating Scrum events, assisting the Product Owner with Backlog management, and coaching the team on self-management and collaboration. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Solving all technical issues for the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not directly solve technical challenges.
answer2: Facilitating Scrum events to ensure they are productive and effective.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating Scrum events is a core responsibility of the Scrum Master.
answer3: Helping the Product Owner manage the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: The Scrum Master supports the Product Owner in refining the Backlog and facilitating stakeholder engagement.
answer4: Coaching the team on self-management and cross-functionality.
explanation4: Correct: Coaching supports the team in becoming more self-sufficient and effective.
answer5: Directing the team’s daily work tasks.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not direct work; the team manages their own tasks.

title: Which artifact helps the team inspect and adapt their progress toward the Sprint Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog provides a detailed plan that allows the team to inspect their progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt as necessary. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog outlines future work but does not specifically help the team inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog helps the team track their progress and make necessary adjustments during the Sprint.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment represents completed work but does not help track ongoing progress.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality but does not help track progress.

title: Which artifact provides visibility into the team’s plan for achieving the Sprint Goal and tracks progress throughout the Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog provides a clear and transparent view of the team’s plan and progress during the Sprint, supporting alignment with the Sprint Goal. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog shows future work but does not provide visibility into the current Sprint’s progress.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog provides transparency into the work planned and tracks progress toward the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment represents completed work but does not show the current plan or progress.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not provide a view of the team’s progress.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is responsible for approving the team's work at the end of each Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner does not approve the Increment; it is considered done when it meets the agreed Definition of Done. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not approve work; the Increment is assessed based on the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner does not approve work; completed items that meet the Definition of Done are considered done.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team finds that one of the items is too complex to complete in a single Sprint. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine complex items, breaking them into smaller, manageable pieces that can be completed within a Sprint. “Product Backlog items that can be Done by the Scrum Team within one Sprint are deemed ready for selection in a Sprint Planning event.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Include the item as-is and hope it can be completed.
explanation1: Incorrect: Including overly complex items without refinement can disrupt the Sprint.
answer2: Work with the team to break down the item into smaller, manageable tasks.
explanation2: Correct: Refining complex items into smaller tasks helps ensure they are actionable and aligned with the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Move the item to the next Sprint without changes.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying work without refinement does not address complexity.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the refinement separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing the refinement process.

title: What is the Product Owner's main responsibility during Sprint Planning? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: During Sprint Planning, the Product Owner provides context and clarity on Product Backlog items, helping the team understand the work. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: To create a detailed plan for the Sprint with the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner focuses on the 'what' not the detailed 'how'.
answer2: To ensure the Developers select enough Product Backlog items to satisfy stakeholders.
explanation2: Incorrect: The team selects items based on capacity, not stakeholder pressure.
answer3: To clarify and provide context for selected Product Backlog items.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner ensures clarity and context for the items chosen for the Sprint.
answer4: To approve the Sprint Backlog created by the Developers.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Developers self-manage the Sprint Backlog, and it does not require approval from the Product Owner.

title: Which three practices help ensure that a Scrum Team consistently delivers value to the stakeholders? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Prioritizing high-value items, conducting Sprint Reviews, and maintaining a relevant Definition of Done help ensure that the Scrum Team consistently delivers value. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
